title: BLF: Fix CAN parsing
description:
CAN_MESSAGE and CAN_MESSAGE2 data is fixed size (8 bytes), but it was treated as variable when reading the CAN_MESSAGE2 trailer

Fix DLC parsing by masking the lower nibble instead of capping the value to 15

notes.body: @LarsVoelker can you take a look at this one too?

added 4 commits
  • 4731e584...b227c21d - 3 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 1f282525 - BLF: Fix CAN parsing
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/12635/diffs?diff_id=818273215&start_sha=4731e584fcb22e73b4abe1e106387d6e125d7281)
I also want to extract the BRS and ESI flags from BLF_OBJTYPE_CAN_FD_MESSAGE and BLF_OBJTYPE_CAN_FD_MESSAGE_64. Should I add the code here, or in another MR?
Mixing enhancements and bugfixes makes it really hard to pull the bugfix into the release branches. So would recommend to not mix enhancements and bugfixes.

And you probably want to also encode the CANFD_FDF flag too.

All three were added after I wrote the code for blf. :(

https://www.tcpdump.org/linktypes/LINKTYPE_CAN_SOCKETCAN.html

This is not the same. MIN(dlc, 15) != mod 16. Is there a reason to assume that mod 16 is better?

In addition, if the payload is only 8 Bytes, we probably should cap at 8, shouldn't we?

The reasoning behind the change is that the DLC field in the CAN message is only 4 bits wide, so anything in the upper nibble (if ever present) is garbage. Of course this is not the same as capping it to 15. And at this point why 15? As you said, 8 would be better.

Maybe we should keep the DLC as is (still mod 16 in my opinion, since we would never see the upper nibble on the wire), adding another parameter to `blf_can_fill_buf_and_rec()`.

My doubt now is if this still counts as bugfix or goes with the other enhancements mentioned above.

As I implemented the payload_length vs payload_length_valid change, I realized that keeping the DLC in the len field doesn't make sense.

So forget about the second part of my comment.
If you say that the buffer is always 8 bytes, does this if-clause still makes sense?

It doesn't. Do you think it's better to just remove the check, or modify the message struct too (like in the LIN case)? The second option would require some changes to `blf_can_fill_buf_and_rec()` too.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/12635/diffs?diff_id=818722407&start_sha=1f28252537bbbb6a3fa308f1fdc344269bc1fb9e#4edaab23888743307322f501fbaef9f54209f5e5_1320_1314)
Also not sure, if it is better to cap or mod.
